- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.50), model often underestimates; adjust downward by 3–7% to avoid missing downside risk.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 2–5% from forecast 3–5 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price decline, model often fails to correct; add 1–3% downward bias to next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon 30d: model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; dampen sensitivity to sentiment > 0.50 by applying a 0.5–1x smoothing factor.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with trend direction; align forecast slope with sentiment momentum (e.g., if sentiment rising, forecast should trend up; if falling, trend down).
